components.note: 羊 (sheep) — 羞 pairs a sheep with the idea of something unsightly.
丑 (ugly, shameful) contributes to the character's form, giving 羞 its meaning 'ashamed, shy.'
忄 (heart) — 愧 describes an emotional state of shame or guilt.
鬼 (guǐ) gives a sound close to kuì, sharing the initial and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 他偷懒被老师发现，感到十分羞愧。
example.pinyin: tā tōulǎn bèi lǎoshī fāxiàn, gǎndào shífēn xiūkuì.
example.english: He felt deeply ashamed after the teacher caught him slacking off.
example.fact: Blushing is one of the few human expressions Charles Darwin called 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions' because no other animal is known to do it involuntarily. It is triggered by adrenaline widening the tiny veins in the face, and studies show people trust a blushing person more, since the reaction is almost impossible to fake.

components.note: 巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.
人 (person), tripled — three people together depict a crowd, giving 众 its meaning 'many, multitude.'

example.hanzi: 政府决定听取民众的意见。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ juédìng tīngqǔ mínzhòng de yìjiàn.
example.english: The government decided to listen to the opinions of the populace.
example.fact: Ancient Athens ran the world's first large-scale direct democracy around 500 BC, where roughly 6,000 citizens could gather in the Assembly to vote directly on laws by show of hands. Ordinary citizens were also chosen by lottery, not election, to fill most government posts, a system meant to prevent any single faction from controlling public office.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 保护幼崽是动物的本能。
example.pinyin: bǎohù yòuzǎi shì dòngwù de běnnéng.
example.english: Protecting their young is an instinct in animals.
example.fact: Sea turtle hatchlings dig out of their sand nests and crawl straight toward the ocean within minutes of birth, without ever having seen water or a parent to guide them. Researchers believe they read the natural slope of the beach and the brighter horizon over open water, an instinct so fixed that artificial lighting near beaches can fatally misdirect them inland.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 这个消息大大提高了大家的信心。
example.pinyin: zhège xiāoxi dàdà tígāo le dàjiā de xìnxīn.
example.english: This news greatly boosted everyone's confidence.
example.fact: The Richter scale for earthquakes is logarithmic, so each whole-number increase represents roughly 32 times more released energy, not merely a linear jump. That is why a magnitude 7 earthquake is not just 'a bit bigger' than a magnitude 6, but releases about 32 times as much energy — a difference vast enough to turn a shaking building into a collapsing one.

components.note: 目 (eye) — supervising, 督's meaning, involves watching closely.
叔 (shū) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading dū has diverged.
宀 (roof) — 察 relates to careful observation
祭 (jì) gives a loose sound connection to 察's reading chá

example.hanzi: 海关督察每天检查进出港的货物。
example.pinyin: hǎiguān dūchá měitiān jiǎnchá jìnchūgǎng de huòwù.
example.english: Customs inspectors check incoming and outgoing cargo every day.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was never a single continuous fortification but a patchwork of walls built by different dynasties over roughly 2,000 years, and it relied on a dense network of watchtowers where guards used smoke signals by day and fire by night to relay warnings of approaching threats across hundreds of miles.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 蔬 names edible plants, vegetables.
疏 (shū) gives the sound — an exact match with 蔬.
艹 (plant) — 菜 names something grown, a vegetable.
采 (cǎi) gives a sound close to cài, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每天都会买新鲜的蔬菜。
example.pinyin: māma měitiān dūhuì mǎi xīnxiān de shūcài.
example.english: Mom buys fresh vegetables every day.
example.fact: Tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers are botanically fruits since they develop from a flower's ovary and contain seeds, yet in 1893 the US Supreme Court ruled in Nix v. Hedden that tomatoes count as vegetables for import-tariff purposes, based on how they are commonly eaten rather than their botanical classification.

components.note: 彡 (hair/decorative strokes) — 修 relates to grooming, decorating, or improving something
攸 (yōu) gives a sound close to 修's reading xiū, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'

example.hanzi: 工程师花了三天时间修复了系统漏洞。
example.pinyin: gōngchéngshī huāle sān tiān shíjiān xiūfù le xìtǒng lòudòng.
example.english: The engineer spent three days fixing the system vulnerability.
example.fact: The Sistine Chapel ceiling restoration, completed in 1994 after over a decade of work, revealed that centuries of candle soot and old varnish had darkened Michelangelo's frescoes so much that restorers had misjudged his palette for generations — the cleaned colors turned out to be far brighter and more vivid than anyone expected.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢画画。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan huàhuà.
example.english: He has liked drawing ever since he was little.
example.fact: Mozart began composing his first pieces of music at age five, and by age six he was performing for European royalty on tours arranged by his father. Modern research on child prodigies suggests such early starts often combine unusual working memory with thousands of hours of deliberate practice packed into the earliest years of life.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match
氵 (water) — relates to 满's meaning 'full,' water filling to the brim.
㒼 (mán) gives a sound hint — 满 is pronounced mǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他把行李箱装满了礼物。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ xínglixiāng zhuāngmǎn le lǐwù.
example.english: He filled the suitcase with gifts.
example.fact: A camel can drink up to 200 liters of water in about three minutes when it finally reaches a water source, rapidly filling its bloodstream and rehydrating tissues that lost significant water weight during its trek. Contrary to popular belief, camels do not store water in their humps — the humps hold fat, which the animal metabolizes for energy on long desert journeys.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā
罒 (an eye) — held open.
又 (a hand) — pulling the eye open wide, together giving 曼 its meaning 'long, extended, graceful.'

example.hanzi: 阿曼位于阿拉伯半岛的东南部。
example.pinyin: Āmàn wèiyú Ālābó bàndǎo de dōngnánbù.
example.english: Oman is located in the southeastern part of the Arabian Peninsula.
example.fact: Oman's Jebel Shams canyon is sometimes called the 'Grand Canyon of Arabia,' plunging roughly 1,000 meters, and the country still uses an ancient irrigation system called aflaj, dating back over 1,500 years, that channels water from mountain springs and underground sources to farms using only gravity.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吓 relates to a shout or cry, as when someone is frightened.
下 (xià) gives the sound — an exact match with 吓.
口 (mouth) — 唬 (to bluff, to intimidate) is done through the mouth, evoking a tiger's roar.
虎 (hǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 唬's reading.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢吓唬弟弟，说房间里有鬼。
example.pinyin: tā xǐhuan xiàhu dìdi, shuō fángjiān lǐ yǒu guǐ.
example.english: He likes to scare his younger brother by saying there's a ghost in the room.
example.fact: Opossums have one of the most famous fear responses in nature: when threatened, they involuntarily collapse, drool, and emit a foul odor while appearing dead for up to several hours, a reflex called thanatosis. It is not a conscious act but an automatic nervous-system shutdown triggered by extreme stress, similar to fainting.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 警方认定这起事故是人为操作失误造成的。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng rèndìng zhè qǐ shìgù shì rénwéi cāozuò shīwù zàochéng de.
example.english: Police determined that the accident was caused by human operational error.
example.fact: The 1986 Chernobyl disaster was ultimately attributed by investigators to a combination of a flawed reactor design and operator error during a poorly planned safety test, when staff disabled key safety systems. The explosion released radioactive material equivalent to hundreds of times more fallout than the atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki combined.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 语 relates to language, words, and speech
吾 (wú) gives a loose sound connection to 语's reading yǔ
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.hanzi: 她说话的语气突然变得严肃起来。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà de yǔqì tūrán biàn de yánsù qǐlái.
example.english: Her tone suddenly became serious.
example.fact: Researchers estimate that in face-to-face communication, tone of voice and body language often carry more emotional meaning than the actual words spoken, a finding popularly (if often oversimplified) traced to psychologist Albert Mehrabian's 1967 studies on how people judge feelings like liking or disliking.

components.note: 匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 此时，太阳正缓缓落下。
example.pinyin: cǐshí, tàiyáng zhèng huǎnhuǎn luòxià.
example.english: At this moment, the sun was slowly setting.
example.fact: A sunset's colors appear because sunlight travels through more atmosphere at a low angle, scattering away most of the blue and violet wavelengths and leaving the reds and oranges to reach our eyes — the same physical process, called Rayleigh scattering, that makes the daytime sky blue in the first place.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
心 (heart/mind) — 忘 relates to something slipping from the mind.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound distantly related to wàng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这是我一生中最难忘的旅行。
example.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ yīshēng zhōng zuì nánwàng de lǚxíng.
example.english: This was the most unforgettable trip of my life.
example.fact: People with highly superior autobiographical memory, a rare condition studied since the mid-2000s, can recall the exact day of the week and personal details for almost every date of their lives, yet brain scans show their memory for unrelated facts, like memorizing random lists, is entirely ordinary.

components.note: A drawing of a left hand holding a tool, contrasted with 又, an early form of the right hand.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 他习惯用左手写字。
example.pinyin: tā xíguàn yòng zuǒshǒu xiězì.
example.english: He is used to writing with his left hand.
example.fact: Left-handed people make up only about 10 percent of the global population, a ratio that has stayed remarkably stable across cultures and centuries. Studies of cave art and ancient tools suggest this same roughly one-in-ten split existed among prehistoric humans tens of thousands of years ago.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 他天天早上都去公园跑步。
example.pinyin: tā tiāntiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
example.english: He goes jogging in the park every morning.
example.fact: Marathon monks of Mount Hiei in Japan undertake a thousand-day challenge in which they run roughly 40 kilometers a day for 100 consecutive days each year, spread over seven years, as an extreme Buddhist practice of physical discipline meant to achieve spiritual enlightenment through repetition.

meanings: (of a product, service, project etc) flagship

components.note: Hand — a fist is a closed hand.
Gives a sound distantly related to quán, having drifted apart over time.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 他紧紧地握着拳头，努力控制自己的情绪。
example.pinyin: tā jǐnjǐn de wòzhe quántou, nǔlì kòngzhì zìjǐ de qíngxù.
example.english: He clenched his fist tightly, trying to control his emotions.
example.fact: The mantis shrimp can snap its clawed forelimb so fast that it creates cavitation bubbles in the water, generating a brief flash of light and heat nearly as hot as the sun's surface, and the resulting shockwave can crack aquarium glass or shatter a snail shell in a single strike.

components.note: 石 (rock) — 碰 originally described one hard object, like a stone, striking another, giving 'to bump, to collide.'
並 (bìng) is only distantly related in sound to pèng — both use a bilabial initial (b/p), but the rhyme and tone have drifted apart.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 我在路上碰上了一个老朋友。
example.pinyin: wǒ zài lùshàng pèngshàng le yī gè lǎo péngyou.
example.english: I ran into an old friend on the road.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, unexpectedly encountered a region of dense interstellar plasma in 2012 as it crossed into interstellar space, a discovery that only happened because the spacecraft's instruments recorded oscillations after a coronal mass ejection from the sun reached it a year later, letting scientists measure the plasma density directly.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 握 describes an action done with the hand: grasping tightly.
屋 (wū) gives a sound distantly related to wò, having drifted apart over time.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 两位领导人在会议开始前握手致意。
example.pinyin: liǎng wèi lǐngdǎorén zài huìyì kāishǐ qián wòshǒu zhìyì.
example.english: The two leaders shook hands before the meeting began.
example.fact: The handshake is believed to have originated as a way to show one was not carrying a weapon, and the up-and-down shaking motion may have started as a check to dislodge any hidden blade from a sleeve — a practical gesture of trust that evolved into today's social greeting.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.
方 (a banner or flag on a pole) — 施 originally related to a flag being unfurled and set in motion.
也 (yě) is close in sound to shī only in its ancient form; the modern readings have drifted apart, though the graphic element is retained.

example.hanzi: 这所学校的体育设施非常齐全。
example.pinyin: zhè suǒ xuéxiào de tǐyù shèshī fēicháng qíquán.
example.english: This school's sports facilities are very well equipped.
example.fact: The International Space Station, humanity's largest inhabited facility in orbit, took over a decade to assemble from 1998 to 2011 using more than 30 missions, and it travels around Earth roughly every 90 minutes, meaning astronauts on board witness about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day.

components.note: 大 (a person) — arms spread, exerting effort.
田 (a field) — working hard on the land, together giving 奋 its meaning 'to strive, exert oneself.'
斗 depicts a hand-held dipper or ladle used for measuring grain and liquids — giving 斗 its meaning 'a unit of dry measure,' and by extension, the Big Dipper constellation.

example.hanzi: 他为了实现自己的梦想不断奋斗。
example.pinyin: tā wèile shíxiàn zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng bùduàn fèndòu.
example.english: He kept striving to achieve his dream.
example.fact: Thomas Edison and his team reportedly tested thousands of different filament materials before settling on a carbonized bamboo fiber that let his light bulb burn for over 1,200 hours, an extreme case of trial-and-error persistence that Edison summarized in his famous remark that genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 这道数学题的难度比想象中要大。
example.pinyin: zhè dào shùxué tí de nándù bǐ xiǎngxiàng zhōng yào dà.
example.english: This math problem is more difficult than expected.
example.fact: The Collatz conjecture, a math problem so simple a child can state it — take any positive number, and if it's even halve it, if odd triple it and add one, repeat — has resisted proof since the 1930s despite being verified by computer for every number up to nearly 2^68, illustrating that a problem's simplicity says nothing about its true difficulty.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抵 describes pushing back or propping something up with the hand.
氐 (dī) gives a sound close to dǐ, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 飞机将于晚上八点抵达机场。
example.pinyin: fēijī jiāng yú wǎnshàng bā diǎn dǐdá jīchǎng.
example.english: The plane will arrive at the airport at eight in the evening.
example.fact: NASA's New Horizons probe took over nine years to arrive at Pluto after launching in 2006, traveling roughly 4.7 billion kilometers, and its brief flyby in 2015 revealed a heart-shaped glacier of nitrogen ice and mountain ranges made of water ice, features no one had expected from a world once dismissed as a frozen, featureless rock.

components.note: Originally a pictograph of a musical bell or instrument hung in a frame; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional word 南, 'south.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 这种气候在南部地区更为常见。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng qìhòu zài nánbù dìqū gèng wéi chángjiàn.
example.english: This type of climate is more common in the southern region.
example.fact: Because Earth is tilted on its axis, the southern hemisphere experiences summer in December and winter in June, exactly opposite the northern hemisphere, and Antarctica in the far south holds about 70 percent of the world's fresh water, locked away as ice.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
禾 (grain) — 秒 originally named the delicate beard of a grain stalk.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound moderately close to miǎo, sharing the rhyme.

example.hanzi: 光在一秒内可以绕地球七圈半。
example.pinyin: guāng zài yī miǎo nèi kěyǐ rào dìqiú qī quān bàn.
example.english: Light can travel around the Earth about seven and a half times in one second.
example.fact: A second is now officially defined not by clocks or the Earth's rotation but by the vibration of a cesium-133 atom, which oscillates exactly 9,192,631,770 times during one second — a definition adopted in 1967 that is so precise modern atomic clocks would lose only about one second every 300 million years.

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
术 depicts a plant with grain hanging from its stalk, related to 木 (tree); it was later borrowed to mean a technique, skill, or art, a sense unrelated to its plant-based origin.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 医生正在手术室里为病人做手术。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zhèngzài shǒushùshì lǐ wèi bìngrén zuò shǒushù.
example.english: The doctor is performing surgery on the patient in the operating room.
example.fact: Before general anesthesia became common in the 1840s, surgeons prized speed above all else — the 19th-century Scottish surgeon Robert Liston reportedly could amputate a leg in under 30 seconds, since faster surgery meant less blood loss and less time for a fully conscious patient to suffer or struggle.

components.note: 彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng

example.hanzi: 科学家发现了一颗新的行星。
example.pinyin: kēxuéjiā fāxiàn le yī kē xīn de xíngxīng.
example.english: Scientists discovered a new planet.
example.fact: As of the mid-2020s, astronomers have confirmed over 5,000 exoplanets orbiting other stars, most detected by watching for the tiny dip in a star's brightness as a planet passes in front of it. One of the strangest finds, WASP-76b, is thought to rain molten iron on its permanent night side after temperatures on its scorching day side vaporize metal.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这个证据非常有力，足以证明他的清白。
example.pinyin: zhège zhèngjù fēicháng yǒulì, zúyǐ zhèngmíng tā de qīngbái.
example.english: This evidence is very compelling, enough to prove his innocence.
example.fact: DNA fingerprinting was first used to solve a criminal case in 1986 in England, when British geneticist Alec Jeffreys's technique both convicted a killer and exonerated a wrongly suspected man, launching forensic DNA analysis as one of the most powerful tools in modern criminal investigation.

components.note: 贝 (money) — gambling involves staking money.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to dǔ, having drifted apart over time.
氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 他在这次投资中下了很大的赌注。
example.pinyin: tā zài zhè cì tóuzī zhōng xiàle hěn dà de dǔzhù.
example.english: He put down a huge stake in this investment.
example.fact: In 1956, Nathan Detroit-style casino math aside, real gambling odds are precisely calculable: the house edge in roulette comes from the single extra zero pocket, giving the casino a mathematical advantage of about 2.7 percent on every spin regardless of how players bet, a built-in edge that guarantees long-run profit for the house.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
氵 (water) — relates directly to 流's meaning 'to flow.'
㐬 (liú) gives the sound — 流 is also pronounced liú, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的服务是一流的。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā cāntīng de fúwù shì yīliú de.
example.english: This restaurant's service is top quality.
example.fact: Switzerland has topped global innovation and competitiveness rankings for years running, a position researchers link to its dense concentration of research institutions like ETH Zurich, its strong vocational-training system, and one of the world's highest rates of patents filed per capita.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 珍 names something precious, like a valuable jewel.
彡 (shān) gives a sound distantly related to zhēn, having drifted apart over time.
忄 (heart) — 惜 describes an emotional response felt in the heart.
昔 (the past, former times) — feeling 忄 for the past 昔 gave 惜 its meaning 'to cherish, to regret.'

example.hanzi: 我们应该珍惜和家人相处的时光。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yīnggāi zhēnxī hé jiārén xiāngchǔ de shíguāng.
example.english: We should cherish the time spent with family.
example.fact: Giant pandas spend up to 14 hours a day eating bamboo just to meet their energy needs, since bamboo is so low in nutrients, yet conservation efforts since the 1980s have helped move the species from endangered to vulnerable status by 2016, one of the rare modern success stories in wildlife protection.

components.note: 戊 (an ancient halberd-like weapon) — 成 pictures a weapon being completed or readied.
丁 (a nail, here suggesting fitting a final piece into place) — combined with the weapon above, this gave 成 its meaning 'to complete, accomplish, succeed.'
田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

example.hanzi: 这项研究的成果得到了广泛认可。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng yánjiū de chéngguǒ dédàole guǎngfàn rènkě.
example.english: The results of this research have been widely recognized.
example.fact: Penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 after he noticed mold had killed bacteria in a forgotten petri dish, was not turned into a usable medicine until over a decade later, when a team led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed methods to mass-produce it in time to treat wounded soldiers during World War II.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 培 originally described banking up soil around a plant's roots, extending to 'to cultivate, nurture.'
咅 (pǒu) gives a sound distantly related to péi, having drifted apart over time.
儿 (child) — 养 relates to raising and nurturing children or animals
羊 (yáng) gives a sound close to 养's reading yǎng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 老师鼓励学生从小培养阅读的习惯。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī gǔlì xuéshēng cóngxiǎo péiyǎng yuèdú de xíguàn.
example.english: Teachers encourage students to cultivate a reading habit from a young age.
example.fact: Petri dishes, invented by German bacteriologist Julius Richard Petri in 1887 while working in Robert Koch's laboratory, remain the standard tool for culturing microorganisms over 130 years later, and the agar gel typically used inside them is derived from red algae, a substance first adopted for lab use in 19th-century Japan.

components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.

example.hanzi: 我们周四下午有一场重要的会议。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zhōusì xiàwǔ yǒu yī chǎng zhòngyào de huìyì.
example.english: We have an important meeting on Thursday afternoon.
example.fact: Thursday is named after Thor, the Norse god of thunder, via the Old English 'Thunresdæg,' mirroring how the Romans named the same day after Jupiter, their own thunder god — a naming pattern found across many European languages that mapped their gods onto the Roman planetary week.

components.note: 止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'
口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

example.hanzi: 古代的先知常常预言未来的灾难。
example.pinyin: gǔdài de xiānzhī chángcháng yùyán wèilái de zāinàn.
example.english: Ancient prophets often foretold future disasters.
example.fact: The Oracle of Delphi in ancient Greece was consulted by kings and commoners alike for centuries, and modern geological studies suggest the priestess's trance-like prophecies may have been influenced by ethylene or other gases seeping up through a fault line beneath the temple, offering a scientific explanation for an ancient religious phenomenon.

components.note: Grain — originally related to arranging harvested grain in order.
Gives the sound shī, related to zhì but drifted apart over time.
广 (a wide building) — 序 relates to arrangement, as in the ordered layout of a hall.
予 (yǔ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though it has diverged from the modern reading xù.

example.hanzi: 维持社会秩序是政府的重要职责。
example.pinyin: wéichí shèhuì zhìxù shì zhèngfǔ de zhòngyào zhízé.
example.english: Maintaining social order is an important responsibility of the government.
example.fact: Ant colonies maintain remarkably strict order without any central leader, coordinating tens of thousands of workers through pheromone trails alone. Studies of ant traffic have found they self-organize to avoid congestion so efficiently that engineers have borrowed their algorithms to improve computer network routing and truck logistics.

components.note: 田 (field) — represents farmland.
力 (strength/effort) — someone strong enough to work the fields gave 男 its meaning 'male, man.'
士 depicts a battle-axe or ceremonial weapon standing upright, an emblem once carried by men serving in official or military roles — giving 士 its meaning 'scholar, gentleman, officer.'

example.hanzi: 这家理发店专门为男士提供服务。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā lǐfàdiàn zhuānmén wèi nánshì tígōng fúwù.
example.english: This barbershop specializes in serving men.
example.fact: The necktie is believed to trace back to Croatian mercenaries serving in France in the 17th century, whose neck scarves caught the eye of French nobility and were adapted into the 'cravat,' the direct ancestor of the modern tie still worn by men in business attire today.

components.note: 开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'
犬 (dog) — an old, now-opaque link behind 状's meaning 'form, shape, condition'
丬 (qiáng) gives a loose sound connection to 状's reading zhuàng

example.hanzi: 这块石头的形状很奇特。
example.pinyin: zhè kuài shítou de xíngzhuàng hěn qítè.
example.english: This stone has a very peculiar shape.
example.fact: Honeycomb cells form hexagons not because bees deliberately choose that shape but because wax naturally settles into hexagons under the physical pressures of surface tension and crowding, the same geometric principle mathematicians proved in the 'honeycomb conjecture' minimizes the material needed to enclose a given amount of space.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
亻 (person) — 倒 relates to a person falling over
到 (dào) gives the sound — 倒 is also pronounced dào, an exact match

example.hanzi: 示威者高呼口号，要求打倒腐败官员。
example.pinyin: shìwēizhě gāohū kǒuhào, yāoqiú dǎdǎo fǔbài guānyuán.
example.english: The protesters shouted slogans, demanding the overthrow of corrupt officials.
example.fact: The fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989 began almost by accident, when an East German official misspoke at a press conference and implied border crossings were opening immediately; crowds rushed the checkpoints that same night, and guards, lacking clear orders, simply let them through.

components.note: 犭 (dog) shows 猎 relates to hunting with animals.
昔 (xī) gives a sound distantly related to liè, having drifted apart over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 这位猎人在森林里追踪野兔的足迹。
example.pinyin: zhè wèi lièrén zài sēnlín lǐ zhuīzōng yětù de zújì.
example.english: This hunter tracked the wild rabbit's footprints in the forest.
example.fact: The San people of the Kalahari Desert practice persistence hunting, chasing an animal like a kudu for hours under the midday sun until it collapses from heatstroke, since humans can dissipate heat through sweating far more efficiently than most four-legged prey, a trait some scientists argue shaped early human evolution.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 悲 relates to a heavy, sorrowful heart.
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to bēi, having drifted apart over time.
Mouth — associated with crying out in grief.
Gives a sound distantly related to āi, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 失去亲人让他感到无比悲哀。
example.pinyin: shīqù qīnrén ràng tā gǎndào wúbǐ bēiāi.
example.english: Losing his loved one made him feel immensely sorrowful.
example.fact: Elephants are among the few non-human animals observed engaging in what researchers call grieving behavior, standing over and touching the bones of dead herd members for extended periods, and some matriarchs have been seen returning to the same site years after a death, long after the bones have weathered away.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 他因为吃了变质的食物而食物中毒。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi chīle biànzhí de shíwù ér shíwù zhòngdú.
example.english: He got food poisoning from eating spoiled food.
example.fact: Botulinum toxin, the substance behind botulism poisoning, is considered one of the most lethal natural substances known, with an estimated lethal dose for humans measured in mere nanograms — yet heavily diluted medical versions of the same toxin are used safely worldwide as Botox to relax muscles and smooth wrinkles.

components.note: 发 (simplified from 發) originally pictured a hand drawing back a bow, the arrow about to be sent flying — giving 发 its meaning 'to send out, to issue, to emit,' as well as 'to develop, grow.'
见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

example.hanzi: 她突然发觉自己把钱包忘在家里了。
example.pinyin: tā tūrán fājué zìjǐ bǎ qiánbāo wàng zài jiālǐ le.
example.english: She suddenly realized she had left her wallet at home.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin's antibacterial power in 1928 happened only because he noticed, almost by chance, that a stray mold spore had drifted into an uncovered petri dish and killed the bacteria growing around it — a moment of realization now considered one of the most important accidents in medical history.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 这条路是私家车道，禁止停车。
example.pinyin: zhè tiáo lù shì sījiā chēdào, jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
example.english: This road is a private driveway; parking is prohibited.
example.fact: Venice has no private cars at all within its historic center, since the city is built across more than 100 small islands linked by canals and roughly 400 bridges, making boats — including private motorboats owned by wealthier residents — the only practical form of personal transport.

components.note: 己 (a kneeling child) — the one being disciplined.
攵 (a hand with a stick) — correcting the child, giving 改 its meaning 'to change, correct, reform.'
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 造's meaning 'to make, build,' an action carried through to completion.
告 (gào) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zào.

example.hanzi: 政府计划改造这片老旧的城区。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ jìhuà gǎizào zhè piàn lǎojiù de chéngqū.
example.english: The government plans to redevelop this old district.
example.fact: The Netherlands has reclaimed roughly 17 percent of its current land area from the sea and lakes using a system of dikes, pumps, and windmills developed over centuries, transforming what was once shallow water into the polders that now hold major cities and farmland below sea level.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — arrows were historically used as a measuring standard, tied to 短's meaning 'short.'
豆 (dòu) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading duǎn has diverged.
衤 (clothes) — 裤 names a piece of clothing, trousers.
库 (kù) gives the sound — an exact match with 裤.

example.hanzi: 夏天的时候，他总是穿短裤出门。
example.pinyin: xiàtiān de shíhou, tā zǒngshì chuān duǎnkù chūmén.
example.english: In summer, he always goes out wearing shorts.
example.fact: Denim, the fabric behind blue jeans and many shorts, was originally developed in the French city of Nîmes, and its name is thought to derive from 'serge de Nîmes.' The indigo dye traditionally used to color it comes from a plant whose pigment must be chemically transformed through oxidation to turn from yellow-green to the familiar deep blue only after the fabric is exposed to air.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跑 describes an action done with the feet, running.
包 (bāo) gives a sound close to pǎo, sharing the same rhyme.
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.hanzi: 他每天早上坚持跑步一个小时。
example.pinyin: tā měitiān zǎoshang jiānchí pǎobù yī gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: He insists on running for an hour every morning.
example.fact: Kenyan long-distance runners, particularly from the Kalenjin ethnic group, have dominated world marathon rankings for decades, and researchers studying the phenomenon point to a combination of factors including training at high altitude around 2,000 meters, which boosts oxygen-carrying red blood cells, along with a culture that has long emphasized running as transportation and sport from childhood.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 傻 describes a state of mind a person is in.
囟 (the top of the head), together with a striking motion below, pictures someone being hit on the head — the odd image behind 傻's meaning 'foolish.'
事 depicts a hand holding a forked instrument used for recording or governing affairs, an ancient tool linked to official duty — the shape came to represent 'a matter, an affair, a thing to be done.'

example.hanzi: 他年轻的时候做过不少傻事。
example.pinyin: tā niánqīng de shíhou zuòguò bùshǎo shǎshì.
example.english: He did quite a few foolish things when he was young.
example.fact: The Darwin Awards, an informal internet tradition started in the early 1990s, humorously chronicled real cases of people who died or were sterilized through spectacularly foolish self-inflicted accidents, framed as a tongue-in-cheek nod to natural selection removing certain behaviors from the gene pool.

components.note: 亻 (person) — pride and arrogance are human traits.
敖 (áo) gives the sound — a close match for ào, differing only in tone.
忄 (heart) — 慢 describes an unhurried state of mind or pace.
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match with 慢.

example.hanzi: 他的傲慢态度让很多同事感到不满。
example.pinyin: tā de àomàn tàidù ràng hěn duō tóngshì gǎndào bùmǎn.
example.english: His arrogant attitude made many colleagues unhappy.
example.fact: The Titanic was marketed before its 1912 maiden voyage as practically unsinkable, and this widely reported overconfidence is often cited alongside the ship's insufficient lifeboats and its captain's decision to maintain high speed through iceberg-laden waters as compounding factors in the disaster that killed over 1,500 people.
